klingon_latin.notes: Star Trek Klingon (tlhIngan Hol) Latin orthography

buy_bear.notes: OVS imperative. mIl'oD = 'type of animal, sabre bear' (n., Klingon for the Galactic Traveler (KGT), Okrand; Klingon's only bear word, also in mIl'oD ngeb 'teddy bear', TalkNow!); yI- = imperative prefix, you (sg) -> him/her/it (TKD 4.1.1); je' = 'buy, purchase' (v., TKD). Literally 'sabre-bear buy-it!'. Sources: boQwI' data (github.com/De7vID/klingon-assistant-data, entries je', mIl'oD); hol.kag.org/page/Pronominal_prefixes.html. No coined words.

klingon_piqad.notes: Star Trek Klingon in pIqaD, encoded in the ConScript Unicode Registry block U+F8D0-U+F8FF (one code point per Klingon letter: tlh, ch, gh, ng and ' are single letters). Drawn with Constructium (Kreative Software, SIL OFL 1.1; see stimuli/fonts/Constructium-LICENSE.txt).

buy_bear.notes: "Buy a bear." Latin transliteration: mIl'oD yIje'. Letters: m I l ' o D / y I j e ' + KLINGON FULL STOP (pIqaD has no exclamation mark). mIl'oD 'type of animal, sabre bear' (KGT); je' 'buy, purchase' (TKD); yI- imperative prefix, 3rd-person singular object (TKD, imperative prefixes). Same sentence as klingon_latin (mIl'oD yIje'!); see its notes for the gloss and sources.

elvish_sindarin.notes: Lord of the Rings Sindarin Elvish Latin transliteration

buy_bear.notes: Neo-Sindarin imperative. bango = imperative of banga- 'to trade, *sell' (N. banga-, Etymologies, root MBAKH 'exchange'; Eldamo word-2211901887): a-verbs change final -a to -o (Eldamo Sindarin imperative, word-3326716807; cf. lasto, edro). Sindarin has no attested 'buy'; 'trade' is the closest attested verb. vedli = medli 'bear, (lit.) honey-eater' (Neo-Sindarin adaptation of N. megli, Ety/LIS, MAT; vetted by Hiswelókë's Sindarin Dictionary; Eldamo word-1873304745) with soft mutation m > v marking the direct object (Eldamo word-2795181045, word-3345651089). Literally 'trade bear!'. No coined words; medli is the community's standard adaptation of Tolkien's megli. The old verb gwedh- means 'to bind'.

elvish_tengwar.notes: Sindarin in Tengwar, Mode of Beleriand (vowels written as full letters, not tehtar). Encoded in the ConScript/UCSUR Tengwar block U+E000-U+E07F as laid out by the Free Tengwar Font Project mapping. Drawn with Constructium (Kreative Software, SIL OFL 1.1; see stimuli/fonts/Constructium-LICENSE.txt).

buy_bear.notes: Same sentence as elvish_sindarin: Bango vedli. Mode of Beleriand, vowels as full letters: umbar (b), osse (a), anga + nasal bar (ng), anna (o) / ampa (v), yanta (e), ando (d), lambe (l), short carrier (i), double pusta (full stop). Medial Sindarin ng is [ŋg], which Beleriand mode writes as anga with a nasalization bar (Björkman, Amanye Tenceli, at.boktypografen.se/teng_beleriand.htm; the nasal bar in this mode is attested in DTS 8). The tengwar crate's Beleriand mode writes ng as ñoldo, which is the final [ŋ] value, so it was not followed here. Code points follow the Free Tengwar Font Project mapping (U+E000-E07F).

elvish_quenya.notes: Lord of the Rings Quenya High Elven Latin transliteration

buy_bear.notes: Quenya imperative: particle á + uninflected verb (Eldamo intro to Quenya 3.4.2). manca- = 'to trade' (ᴹQ. manka-, Etymologies, root MBAKH 'exchange'; Eldamo word-1807802113). Quenya has no Tolkien-attested 'buy'; the Neo-Quenya homanca- 'to buy' (Fauskanger, built from hó- + manca-; Eldamo word-3134824731) was not used because it is a neologism. morco = 'bear' (ᴹQ. morko, Etymologies, root MOROK; Eldamo word-1805133179). Literally 'do trade bear!'. No coined words. The old verb manta- means 'to bless'.

vulcan.notes: Star Trek Vulcan conlang Latin transliteration

buy_bear.notes: Golic Vulcan (Vulcan Language Institute, Mark R. Gardner). Verb-first imperative. mahr'uh = normal imperative of mahr-tor 'buy, purchase (v.)' (VLI Vulcan-English dictionary, vli.surak.nu/gv-eng4.html): weak -tor verbs take root + 'uh (VLI Lesson 20, vli.surak.nu/lesson20.php). sehlat = 'large bear-like animal (sometimes domesticated as a pet)' (VLI, vli.surak.nu/gv-eng5.html; also canon Star Trek, TAS 'Yesteryear'). Literally 'buy sehlat'. SUBSTITUTION: VLI's English-Vulcan side lists 'ber' for the animal bear, but it is a transparent English loan and does not appear on the Vulcan-English side, so the canon bear-like sehlat is used instead. The old word ha'kiv means 'life'.

Na'vi (Paul Frommer). The imperative is the bare verb with no affix and no subject (Wikibooks Na'vi/Verbs: 'Kä!' 'go!'). kanom = 'acquire, get' (v:tr). yoa = 'in exchange for' (adp.). txolar = 'dollar' (n., a Frommer loanword). Frommer's own way to say 'buy' is kanom + yoa + currency: 'we can adapt kanom + yoa in a natural way to talk about buying things', and he says the currency must be stated (naviteri.org/2014/02/barter-and-exchange/; entries via Reykunyu). COINED: pxer 'bear', a loanword from English 'bear'. Na'vi has no b, so voiced b becomes ejective px, as Frommer turned dollar into txolar (d > tx). Na'vi has no bear or Earth-animal word, and Reykunyu has no 'pxer' entry. pxerit = pxer + accusative -it (after a consonant). Literally 'acquire bear-ACC in-exchange-for dollar!'. The old word sung means 'add'.

high_valyrian.notes: Game of Thrones High Valyrian Latin orthography

buy_bear.notes: High Valyrian (David J. Peterson). LOWEST CONFIDENCE: needs review. gryves = 'bear', inferred from Peterson's blog post title 'Gryves se Riña Litse' = 'The Bear and the Maiden Fair' (dothraki.com/2013/05/gryves-se-rina-litse/; riña 'maiden' and litse 'fair' per Wiktionary Appendix:High_Valyrian). The post never glosses gryves on its own, and the Linguifex entry is a fan wiki and could not be read. gryvī = accusative singular, INFERRED from the solar 4th-declension -es paradigm (zaldrīzes > zaldrīzī, Wiktionary); gryves' own declension class is unattested. SUBSTITUTED VERB: ademmās = singular imperative of ademmagon 'to pay; to fulfil' (Wiktionary Appendix:High_Valyrian/ademmagon; the imperative pattern matches Peterson's limagon > limās, dothraki.com/2013/05/some-high-valyrian-inflection/). No HV buy/sell/trade verb was found, and the argument structure of ademmagon (thing paid for vs. debt) is unattested. Object-verb order (HV order is flexible). Literally 'bear-ACC pay!'. The old word kelih is unattested (cf. keligon 'to stop').

dothraki.notes: Game of Thrones Dothraki Latin orthography

buy_bear.notes: Dothraki (David J. Peterson), verb-first command. jeras = informal imperative of jerat 'to trade' (DP; Dothraki Language Dictionary v3.11, dothraki.org; cf. jerak 'trader, merchant'). Imperative ending inferred from Peterson's lanat > lanas (informal) / lani (formal) (dothraki.com/2013/03/run-like-a-stallion/); jeras itself is not attested. Dothraki has no attested 'buy'; 'trade' is the closest attested verb, and it is unattested whether jerat takes the goods as its object. hlizifes = accusative of hlizif 'bear' (DP, animate; dothraki.com/?p=600): animate nouns take accusative -es (LCS grammar notes, conlang.org/?p=2810). Literally 'trade bear!'. No coined words. The old word arakh means 'curved sword'.

Mando'a (Karen Traviss). ke = imperative prefix 'used as order' with the full -ir verb, as in 'Ke narir haar'ke'gyce rol'eta resol!' (Execute Order 66!). verborir = 'hire, buy, contract'. Both from the Traviss dictionary as hosted on mandoa.org. COINED: ori'ulik 'bear', lit. 'big beast', from ori 'big, extreme, very' + ulik 'mount, pack animal', joined with an apostrophe as in ori'vod 'big brother' and ori'tsad 'brigade'. Mando'a has no attested bear or general 'animal' word. No article: Mando'a rarely uses one (eyn 'a' is marked rare). Literally 'buy big-beast!'. The old word ba'jur means 'education'.

buy_bear.notes: Not a real translation: Simlish has no fixed vocabulary, so this is gibberish ('Dag dag') plus the English word 'bear'. Whether Simlish counts as a representation is pending a decision on issue #15. Left unchanged and exempt from the English-word test until then.
